480	He steered the ship wherever he wanted. He told him: now go right, go left, turn
481	right, right again, left again, stop! Throw the anchor. They threw the
482	anchor. He said, bring me a bucket. They brought a bucket, lowered the bucket
483	into the water and drew up a bucket of water. The elderly
484	Kabbalist, Rav Kaduri, told them: now each one take a cup of this water.
485	This is Miriam's well. Drink, so that you become like an ever-strengthening spring.
486	We blessed "shehakol nihyeh bidvaro." They were thirsty, since if they weren't thirsty one doesn't bless.
487	We blessed "shehakol nihyeh bidvaro" and we drank. Each one took a cup of
488	two revi'it, and we drank. I asked him: so, and how was the taste of
489	the water? Did you think of something else? He said to me: I didn't know you could think of something else. So it stayed the taste of
490	water. Nobody knew this, but at least I had a sign to show whether it was real, because the Rav Chida writes that if
491	you think of the taste of something else, another drink, it has the taste of that drink, and if you think of nothing, it's the taste of
492	water. They didn't think of anything, so it was the taste of water. So I asked him: so,
493	Chacham Moshe, do you remember since then everything you learn?
494	He said to me: HaShem have mercy on us. I didn't understand what that answer was.
495	Does he remember or not?
496	What is "HaShem have mercy" or "not have mercy"?
497	I thought, maybe he says this out of humility?
498	Maybe he doesn't want to tell?
499	I said to him: what is this, "HaShem have mercy"?
500	He said: HaShem have mercy on us.
501	Fine, I understood.
502	From that day I kept an eye on him in the yeshiva.
503	I said, I'll check on him to see whether it truly worked for them or not.
504	Then I would come and ask him all kinds of questions.
505	Like this, not, heaven forbid, to test him.
506	Only to see.
507	Not to test.
508	To check.
509	And I asked him, and apparently it truly did not work for them.
510	So what will you say, that Rav Kaduri just brought them water to drink for nothing?
511	I don't think so.
512	So how can this be?
513	Rather, what?
514	The water that brings a person memory is only an aid, only an addition, but it doesn't
515	make you remember completely.
516	Therefore, if afterward all kinds of things arise, forgetfulness over time, or anger, or pressure,
517	it could be that the water truly won't help, and so they said "I forgot."
518	And this may be the reason how Moshe Rabbeinu forgot.
519	Why?
520	Because situations of anger arose, and the water helps only in a way
521	that a person merits, and apparently it did not work for them.
522	The Rav Chida asks: the Manna that Israel ate in the desert turned into any taste.
523	If he thought of a pig, would it turn into pig or not?
524	What do you say?
525	What?
526	Again: the manna turned into any taste in the world. If he thought of lobster,
527	thought of pig, of calamari, of nigiri, would it become the taste of pig or not?
528	So the Rav Chida brings the Gemara in Chulin 109, page b, and he says that the taste of a forbidden thing
529	is permitted. Where is the taste of a forbidden thing permitted?
530	Where did we see it?
531	The shibuta fish, and they say this fish has the taste of pig. I heard
532	that they found this fish and tasted it, and they say it has the taste of pig.
533	I don't know.
534	You need a pig, you need someone who has tasted pig, you also need to really find out...
535	whether it truly...
536	Today all the flavors are the same.
537	But I don't know.
538	So you see that the taste of pig is permitted.
539	So there is a practical difference in our days, in the United States, here there isn't this.
540	All kinds of kosher foods that have the taste of pig, or the taste of
541	lobster.
542	So in the responsa Minchat Elazar, part 1, siman 68, there he was in doubt whether the taste of a forbidden thing is permitted.
543	And from here is proof that the taste is permitted, as the Gemara brings that the taste of a forbidden thing is permitted. So if the taste is permitted,
544	one can say that if they thought of lobster it would turn into lobster, and if they thought of
545	pig it would turn into the taste of pig. That is, it would be bread with the taste of pig,
546	bread with the taste of lobster. So they would bless "hamotzi." The Gaon Yavetz writes:
547	not "hamotzi lechem min ha'aretz" but "Behold, I will rain down for you bread from heaven." They would bless on it "hamotzi lechem
548	min hashamayim," not from the earth. It came from above, not from below. And then they would eat bread
549	with the taste of pig.
550	Apparently this is difficult for the Rav Chida. In Midrash Talpiyot, Anaf Yayin, he asks: Nadav and Avihu were liable to death.
551	Why?
552	Because they served while intoxicated with wine.
553	Where did they get wine in the desert?
554	Moshe, where did they get wine in the desert?
555	They didn't bring it from the six days of Creation.
556	So tell me, where did they have wine in the desert?
557	He says, the Rav Chida writes, in Devash LePi, Maarechet Ayin, 3, that they thought of
558	the well, they drank from Miriam's well, they thought of wine and became drunk.
559	Wait, wait, wait, wait, hey, oh, oh, oh, oh, so did it turn into wine,
560	or did it turn into water with the taste of wine?
561	Do you understand what I'm asking?
562	If it turned into water with the taste of
563	wine, what would the blessing be?
564	"Shehakol", since it's only water, flavored, like water with flavors, like spring water with flavors.
565	So it's only water. But if it turned into actual wine, what is the blessing?
566	"Borei peri hagafen." So it must be that it turned into actual wine,
567	because they became drunk. You don't get drunk from water with the taste of wine, you get drunk from wine.
568	So if it turned into actual wine, then why, when they thought of pig, did it
569	turn only into bread with the taste?
570	Why didn't it turn into actual pig?
571	Do you understand the question?
572	A huge question.
573	And Rabbi Yosef Engel writes in Gilyonei HaShas, that since, in Berachot
574	48b, it is proven that the wine turns into wine.
575	The water would turn into wine.
576	So this is a question from our side.
577	So there is one who will see this, and so it also seemed to my humble mind, that when you think of
578	something forbidden, it would turn into the taste of it.
579	But when you think of something permitted, it would turn into the permitted thing itself.
580	If they thought of chicken, it would turn into actual chicken, and its blessing would be "shehakol."
581	But if they thought of pig, it would turn into bread with the taste of pig.
582	Do you understand the point?
583	So now, is wine permitted or forbidden to drink?
584	It is permitted to drink wine.
585	And therefore they would drink the water thinking of wine, and then they would drink a lot of wine and
586	become drunk, and so they served while intoxicated with wine.
587	Because the Holy One, blessed be He, would not bring a stumbling block through the gift He gave to Israel.
588	So when they thought of something forbidden, it would turn only into the taste of it, and when they thought
589	of something permitted, it would turn into the thing itself.
590	And so it can be resolved.
591	Some asked: how did they have wine libations on the altar in the desert for 40 years?
592	What will you say, that the altar thought of the taste of wine?
593	A difficulty.
594	Moshe, how do you resolve it, Moshe?
595	Did they have fruit?
596	Did they squeeze it for libations?
597	But if you say they had fruit and squeezed it for libations, then the wine was already there.
598	So why do you need to reach this casuistry, that they drank the water and thought of wine,
599	if they really already had fruit?
